questions.question: 1. At the end of the First World War, aims mentioned by Woodrow Wilson of USA included:
options: c. Formation of League of Nations
questions.answer_guide: The best-known of Wilson's Fourteen Points is the formation of a League of Nations (point 14). Strictly, all four options appear in the Fourteen Points (Belgium – 7, Italian frontiers – 9, Poland – 13), so the question is weak. [Check against the official key.]

questions.section: PART TWO: Structured Questions (60 Marks) – Answer all the following questions. Each question carries 6 marks
questions.question: 1. Discuss Three Main Factors which helped early world civilizations to thrive. (6 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
Any three, discussed:
• Rivers and fertile soils – e.g. the Nile, Tigris–Euphrates, Indus – provided water for irrigation and rich farmland, producing surplus food.
• Agriculture and food surplus – allowed population growth, specialisation of labour and the rise of towns.
• Strong government and organisation – kings/priests organised irrigation, defence, laws and taxation.
• Invention of writing and record-keeping (cuneiform, hieroglyphics) and advances in mathematics and science.
• Trade and transport links (rivers, the wheel, boats) which spread goods and ideas.
• Religion that united people and favourable climate/security of natural barriers.

questions.section: PART TWO: Structured Questions (60 Marks) – Answer all the following questions. Each question carries 6 marks
questions.question: 2. Briefly explain Any Three Achievements of Omer Ibnal Khatab during his rule of the Muslim Empire. (6 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
Any three:
• Expanded the empire – conquered Syria, Jerusalem, Iraq, Persia and Egypt.
• Introduced the Hijri calendar (dating from the Hijra).
• Set up the Diwan (public treasury/register) and paid pensions and salaries from the Bayt al-Mal.
• Organised administration: divided the empire into provinces with governors, appointed judges (qadis) and separated the judiciary.
• Founded new garrison cities (Basra, Kufa, Fustat) and built/extended mosques.
• Established police, a postal system and night patrols; was famed for justice and care for the poor.

questions.section: PART TWO: Structured Questions (60 Marks) – Answer all the following questions. Each question carries 6 marks
questions.question: 3. Briefly discuss Any Three Causes for the outbreak of the First World War. (6 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
Any three:
• The alliance system – Triple Alliance (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Italy) vs Triple Entente (Britain, France, Russia) drew many countries into war.
• Militarism and the arms race – especially the Anglo-German naval race.
• Imperialism – rivalry for colonies and markets (e.g. Moroccan crises).
• Nationalism – e.g. Serbian/Slav nationalism in the Balkans, French desire to recover Alsace-Lorraine.
• The immediate cause: the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo (28 June 1914).

questions.section: PART TWO: Structured Questions (60 Marks) – Answer all the following questions. Each question carries 6 marks
questions.question: 4. Analyze Three Results of Somouri Toure's resistance wars against France. (6 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
Any three:
• Samori Touré was captured (1898) and exiled to Gabon, where he died (1900).
• The Mandinka empire collapsed and was incorporated into French West Africa.
• Heavy loss of life, destruction of towns and farms, famine and depopulation (his scorched-earth policy).
• Delayed the French conquest of the Western Sudan for about 16 years.
• Became a symbol of African resistance and inspired later nationalist movements (e.g. in Guinea).

questions.section: PART TWO: Structured Questions (60 Marks) – Answer all the following questions. Each question carries 6 marks
questions.question: 5. Discuss Any Three Terms of Camp David Peace Agreement between Israel and Egyptian governments. (6 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
Any three:
• Israel agreed to withdraw from the Sinai Peninsula and return it to Egypt (completed 1982).
• Egypt recognised the State of Israel and the two countries established full diplomatic relations.
• Israeli ships were guaranteed free passage through the Suez Canal and the Straits of Tiran.
• Sinai was to be demilitarised with UN/multinational forces stationed there.
• A framework for Palestinian autonomy in the West Bank and Gaza was to be negotiated.

questions.section: PART TWO: Structured Questions (60 Marks) – Answer all the following questions. Each question carries 6 marks
questions.question: 6. Evaluate Any Three Effects of the Cold War. (6 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
Any three:
• The arms race and nuclear threat – huge spending on nuclear and conventional weapons.
• Division of the world into two blocs – NATO vs Warsaw Pact; division of Germany and Berlin (Berlin Wall).
• Proxy wars in the Third World – Korea, Vietnam, Afghanistan, Angola, the Horn of Africa (Ogaden war).
• Space race and technological advances.
• Weakened the UN (veto deadlock) and gave rise to the Non-Aligned Movement.
• Superpower aid and support for dictators in developing countries.

questions.section: PART TWO: Structured Questions (60 Marks) – Answer all the following questions. Each question carries 6 marks
questions.question: 7. Identify Any Three Major organs of the United Nations Organization. (6 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
Any three:
• The General Assembly – all member states, one vote each; discusses world issues and approves the budget.
• The Security Council – 15 members (5 permanent with veto); responsible for international peace and security.
• The Secretariat – headed by the Secretary-General; runs the UN's day-to-day work.
• The International Court of Justice – at The Hague; settles legal disputes between states.
• The Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) – co-ordinates economic, social and humanitarian work.
• The Trusteeship Council – supervised trust territories (now suspended).

questions.section: PART TWO: Structured Questions (60 Marks) – Answer all the following questions. Each question carries 6 marks
questions.question: 8. Discuss Three Major Challenges faced by African states after independence. (6 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
Any three:
• Political instability – military coups, civil wars and one-party dictatorships.
• Border disputes inherited from colonial boundaries.
• Economic problems – poverty, foreign debt, dependence on raw-material exports and on former colonial powers (neo-colonialism).
• Tribalism/ethnic conflicts and refugee crises.
• Shortage of skilled manpower, illiteracy, disease and natural disasters (drought, famine).
• Cold War interference by the superpowers.

questions.section: PART TWO: Structured Questions (60 Marks) – Answer all the following questions. Each question carries 6 marks
questions.question: 9. Outline Three Major factors which led to the rise of Somaliland Nationalism. (6 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
Any three:
• Opposition to colonial rule – British taxation, land policies and restrictions on movement.
• Influence of the Dervish resistance of Sayyid Mohamed Abdulle Hassan as an early symbol of resistance.
• Western and Islamic education producing educated leaders.
• The Second World War – Somali soldiers returned with new ideas; the Atlantic Charter promoted self-determination.
• Formation of political organisations (Somaliland National Society, SNL, USP) and the press.
• The handing over of the Haud and Reserved Area to Ethiopia (1954), which united Somalis in protest.
• Independence movements elsewhere in Africa and Asia.

questions.section: PART TWO: Structured Questions (60 Marks) – Answer all the following questions. Each question carries 6 marks
questions.question: 10. Describe Any Three Factors that persuaded Europeans to scramble for Africa in 1884 (6 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
Any three:
• Economic – need for raw materials, new markets for manufactured goods and areas to invest surplus capital after the Industrial Revolution.
• Political – national prestige and power rivalry among European states (e.g. after German and Italian unification).
• Strategic – control of key routes such as the Suez Canal and the Cape route.
• Social – settlement of surplus population and unemployed people.
• Humanitarian/religious – spreading Christianity and 'civilisation', and stopping the slave trade.
• Reports of explorers and missionaries about Africa's wealth; the Berlin Conference (1884–85) set the rules for partition.
